 Galveston County District Court
 Cause No. 2024-CV-0024
 Richard Smith, Plaintiff, v. Harbor Point Mutual Auto Insurance, Defendant
 Plaintiff's Original Petition
Filed:
November 4, 2024
Plaintiff's counsel:
Kyle Sanders, Marshall & Dominguez LLP
PARTIES
Plaintiff Richard Smith is an individual residing in Texas who was the driver and sole occupant of a passenger vehicle involved
in the collision described below. Defendant is an automobile insurance company authorized to write policies in the State of
Texas, which issued the liability and uninsured/underinsured motorist coverage under which Palintiff now seeks recovery.
Defendant may be served through its registered agent in accordance with the Texas Rules of Civil Procedure.
FACTS
On February 23, 2024, Plaintiff was lawfully operating his vehicle on a roadway in League City, Texas, traveling in the lane he
was entitled to occupy. An insured driver operating a vehicle in the adjacent lane attempted to change lanes without first
confirming that the lane was clear. The insured vehicle moved into Plaintiff's lane and sideswiped the side of Plaintiff's vehicle,
forcing it toward the shoulder and causing body and frame damage. Plaintiff did not have a reasonable opportunity to avoid the
impact. Plaintiff reported the collision to Defendant and submitted a claim under the applicable coverage.
NEGLIGENCE
The insured driver owed Plaintiff and other motorists a duty to exercise ordinary care when changing lanes, including checking
mirrors, signaling, and confirming that the movement could be made safely. The insured driver breached that duty by changing
lanes into an occupied lane. Defendant, as the insurer responsible for indemnifying its insured and for evaluating coverage for
Plaintiff's losses, has a duty to handle the claim in good faith and in compliance with the Texas Insurance Code, and Plaintiff
alleges that Defendant has failed to do so by delaying and undervaluing the claim.
DAMAGES
As a direct result of the collision, Plaintiff suffered a neck strain and a back strain, with pain, stiffness, limited range of motion,
and headaches. Plaintiff has incurred medical expenses for examination and treatment and has lost time from work and daily
activities. Plaintiff will likely continue to experience pain and reduced function in the future. Plaintiff seeks actual damages,
including past and future medical expenses, lost earnings, property damage, pain and metnal anguish, and such other relief as the
Court deems just, in an amount of $32,000.00.
